chunks: Al-Qasim from Ali from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily people will pass over the Bridge in ranks, and the Bridge is thinner than hair and the edge of a sword. Some will pass like lightning, some like a galloping horse, some sliding along, some crawling, some walking, and some hanging from it, with fire taking part of him and leaving part.

key_terms.الصِّرَاط: The Bridge of Paradise that all must cross on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.حَبْوًا: Crawling on hands and knees, indicating a slower pace
key_terms.طَبَقَاتٍ: Ranks or groups, indicating different levels of speed and status
key_terms.عَدْوِ الْفَرَسِ: The galloping of a horse, indicating a fast pace
key_terms.مُعَلَّقًا: Hanging, indicating those who are partially saved but partially consumed by fire

ai.seo_question: How will people cross the Sirat bridge on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Abu Basir from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), elaborates on the eschatological reality of al-Ṣirāṭ, emphasizing its dual nature of being finer than hair yet sharper than a sword. It categorizes humanity into distinct ranks based on their spiritual state, ranging from the swift passage of the righteous to the partial consumption of the mediocre, reflecting the Shia scholarly understanding of graded accountability. The mention of varying postures—running, crawling, or hanging—underscores the physical manifestation of one's inner moral condition during the final reckoning.
